patch.value: Correct a wrong shebang claim in the attestation launcher, and bring the canonical auditor up to date

Two problems, and the second explains the first.

The launcher docstring said the auditor 'treats any file whose first two bytes are a shebang as executable shell'. Reproduced against the auditor this repository now consumes, that is false: a shebang says a file executes, it does not say it executes AS shell, so only a shebang naming a shell interpreter makes the body shell input. Written into a throwaway git repository and run through verify(): #!/bin/bash and #!/usr/bin/env sh report the file by name; #!/usr/bin/env node and no shebang do not.

The claim was TRUE for pm-ops 2026.9.5, which this repository was still pinned to - two releases behind the canonical auditor, and therefore missing every fail-open construction closed since. Bumping to ^2026.9.7 is what makes the corrected claim correct, which is why the two changes belong together rather than as a docstring tidy.

The same wrong sentence is in all seven repositories carrying this launcher; it was propagated by copying the reference file, so the error travelled with the text. Corrected in the six sibling convergence branches at the same time.

Also re-exports auditPublishAttestation and verify by reference. The launcher previously exported only runIfMain, so the fleet's bypass-corpus harness read this repository as broken rather than as converged, and no test asserted that what the launcher exposes IS the package's function rather than a wrapper.
The shebang claim is reproduced in the suite, including the two negative cases; The corpus reads the same seven cases as every other converged repository
